chunks.arabic_text: أَبِي رَحِمَهُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ السَّائِحِ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ بْنِ مُوسَىٰ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ ع قَالَ

translations.en: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ali ibn al-Sa'ih from Abdullah ibn Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ يَعْلَمَانِ ٱلذَّنْبَ إِذَا أَرَادَ ٱلْعَبْدُ أَنْ يَفْعَلَهُ أَوْ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ قَالَ فَقَالَ ع أَ فَرِيحُ ٱلْكَنِيفِ وَ ٱلطِّيبِ عِنْدَكَ وَاحِدَةٌ قَالَ قُلْتُ لَا قَالَ ع ٱلْعَبْدُ إِذَا هَمَّ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ خَرَجَ نَفَسُهُ طَيِّبَ ٱلرِّيحِ فَقَالَ صَاحِبُ ٱلْيَمِينِ لِصَاحِبِ ٱلشِّمَالِ قِفْ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ هَمَّ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَإِذَا هُوَ فَعَلَهَا كَانَ لِسَانُهُ قَلَمَهُ وَ رِيقُهُ مِدَادَهُ فَيُثْبِتُهَا لَهُ وَ إِذَا هَمَّ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ خَرَجَ نَفَسُهُ مُنْتِنَ ٱلرِّيحِ فَيَقُولُ صَاحِبُ ٱلشِّمَالِ لِصَاحِبِ ٱلْيَمِينِ قِفْ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ هَمَّ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَإِذَا هُوَ فَعَلَهَا كَانَ لِسَانُهُ قَلَمَهُ وَ رِيقُهُ مِدَادَهُ فَيُثْبِتُهَا عَلَيْهِ

translations.en: I asked him about the two angels who know the sin if the servant intends to do it, or the good deed. He said: Is the smell of the toilet and the perfume the same for you? I said: No. He said: When the servant intends a good deed, his breath comes out sweet-smelling, so the companion of the right says to the companion of the left, 'Stop, for he has intended a good deed.' If he does it, his tongue is his pen and his saliva is his ink, so it is recorded for him. And when he intends an evil deed, his breath comes out foul-smelling, so the companion of the left says to the companion of the right, 'Stop, for he has intended an evil deed.' If he does it, his tongue is his pen and his saliva is his ink, so it is recorded against him.

en.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia* highlights the metaphysical reality of the Kiraman Katibin, emphasizing that their recording begins with the internal state (himma) of the servant, not merely the physical act. The analogy of scent serves as a tangible sign of spiritual purity or corruption, illustrating the Shia concept that intention carries ontological weight in the divine ledger. This underscores the importance of self-monitoring (muhasaba) before action, as the angels' command to 'wait' (qif) indicates a pause in the finalization of the record until the deed is actualized.
en.seo_question: How do the recording angels know a person's intention before they act?

key_terms.رِيحُ ٱلْكَنِيفِ: The smell of the toilet (foul odor)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ ٱلْيَمِينِ: The companion of the right (angel recording good deeds)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ ٱلشِّمَالِ: The companion of the left (angel recording bad deeds)
